1	// andesim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andesim [<cmd>] [--mode M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// `run` is the default command: when the first token is not a known
9	// subcommand (and not a top-level help flag), the whole line parses as
10	// `run ...`, so `andesim --mode fast prog.elf` works without typing `run`.
11	//
12	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
13	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
14	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`cycle` forward an engine's whole
15	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
16	#ifndef ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
17	#define ANDESIM_CLI_HPP
18	
19	#include <string>
20	#include <string_view>
21	#include <vector>
22	
23	namespace andes_sim {
24	
25	// True for the known command names (run/list/doctor/profile). The single
26	// source of truth shared by the parser (default-command rule) and main's
27	// dispatch.
28	bool is_subcommand(std::string_view name);
29	
30	struct Cli {
31	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
32	  std::string model;                      // --mode fast|cycle|hybrid (field stays 'model': the concept, see list models)
33	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
34	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger marker|pc
35	  // Hybrid trigger args (empty => cmd_run applies the default). pc boundaries
36	  // are a symbol name or 0x address; the sizes stay strings here and are
37	  // parsed where they are used.
38	  std::string pc_start;                   // --pc-start (trigger pc)
39	  std::string pc_end;                     // --pc-end   (trigger pc)
40	  std::string mem_size;                   // --mem-size (guest memory; --mmap-size is a hidden alias)
41	  std::string runtime;                    // --runtime linux (proxy-kernel payload; "" => bare-metal ELF, the default)
42	  std::string kanata;                     // --kanata <file> (marker/pc ROI trace)
43	  std::string objdump;                    // --objdump <file> (kanata labels)
44	  std::string log_level;                  // --log-level 0..6 (vsim scale; "" => info)
45	  std::string log_file;                   // --log-file <path> (full trace capture)
46	  std::string step_timeout_ms;            // --step-timeout-ms (hybrid per-leg spawn timeout; "" => PlanOptions' 90000)
47	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
48	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
49	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
50	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
51	  bool print_memmap = false;              // --print-memmap (run --mode hybrid)
52	  bool verify = false;                    // --verify (run --mode hybrid)
53	  bool gdb = false;                       // --gdb (fast: QEMU gdbstub; cycle: vsim JTAG + ICEman)
54	  std::string gdb_port;                   // --gdb-port (fast: default 1234; cycle: default 9104)
55	  // profile's report knobs (values stay strings; cmd_profile applies the
56	  // defaults where they are used, like mem_size/gdb_port above).
57	  std::string limit;                      // --limit (profile; "" => 50)
58	  std::string min_iters;                  // --min-iters (profile; "" => 1)
59	  std::string addr2line;                  // --addr2line (profile; "" => auto)
60	  bool raw = false;                       // --raw (profile: dump the plugin log)
61	  bool llm = true;                        // --llm / --no-llm (profile report format)
62	  bool optimize_rvv = true;               // --optimize-rvv / --no-optimize-rvv (profile)
63	  bool no_source = false;                 // --no-source (profile: skip addr2line)
64	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
65	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
66	};
67

69	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().

73	}  // namespace andes_sim

75	#endif  // ANDESIM_CLI_HPP

2	//
3	// A linux-runtime run boots a per-run COPY of vlinux.elf (the U1 proxy
4	// kernel) whose .manifest section has been stamped with this run's app path
5	// + mem size via `objcopy --update-section`. The app ELF itself is never
6	// booted directly -- vlinux loads it (from U3 onward).

12	#include <vector>

17	// struct vlinux_manifest) for one linux-runtime run. `app_path` must fit the
18	// struct's fixed-size field (incl. NUL terminator); on overflow returns {}
19	// and sets err. `extra_argv` becomes the app's argv[1..] (argv[0] is always
20	// app_path) -- more than VLINUX_MANIFEST_ARGV_MAX_COUNT entries, or entries
21	// whose encoded (NUL-separated) bytes exceed VLINUX_MANIFEST_ARGV_BYTES, is
22	// an error, same no-silent-truncation discipline as the app_path overflow
23	// case.

25	                                         uint64_t mem_size,
26	                                         const std::vector<std::string>& extra_argv,
27	                                         std::string& err);

29	// The `objcopy --update-section` argv that stamps `blob_path`'s bytes into
30	// `vlinux_elf`'s .manifest section, in place. Pure -- testable without
31	// spawning.
32	std::vector<std::string> manifest_objcopy_argv(const std::string& objcopy_bin,
33	                                               const std::string& blob_path,
34	                                               const std::string& vlinux_elf);
35

37	// runtime/linux/vlinux.elf into a fresh temp workdir as vlinux-run.elf, write
38	// the manifest blob, and objcopy --update-section it in place. Needs

44	// same way run_plan's own staged qemu.cfg is never revisited post-spawn).
45	// Returns the staged ELF's path, or "" and sets `err`.
46	std::string stage_linux_runtime(const std::string& app_elf_abs,
47	                                uint64_t mem_size,
48	                                const std::vector<std::string>& extra_argv,
49	                                std::string& err);
50	
51	}  // namespace andes_sim
52	
53	#endif  // ANDESIM_MANIFEST_HPP

1	// ELF symbol resolution for pc-trigger boundaries (F9).
2	//
3	// pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs. Either boundary may be a
4	// "0x"-prefixed hex address (used verbatim) OR a symbol defined in the ELF
5	// (resolved against its .symtab). This decouples the switch points from the
6	// workload source -- any function can bound the ROI, with no planted markers.
7	//
8	// C++ port of tests/lib/roi.sh:resolve_pc, reading the ELF .symtab directly via
9	// <elf.h> rather than shelling out to `nm`.
10	#ifndef ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
11	#define ANDESIM_ELF_SYMS_HPP
12	
13	#include <cstdint>
14	#include <string>
15	
16	namespace andes_sim {
17	
18	// Resolve a pc-mode boundary to a bare hex address string (no "0x" prefix).
19	//   "0x<h>" / "0X<h>"  -> "<h>" verbatim (prefix stripped, digits unchanged)
20	//   <symbol>           -> the symbol's st_value as lowercase hex
21	// On any failure (undefined symbol, unreadable/!ELF file) returns "" and sets
22	// `err` to a message naming the boundary; on success leaves `err` empty.
23	std::string resolve_pc(const std::string& elf_path, const std::string& boundary,
24	                       std::string& err);
25	
26	// The ELF class width in bits from e_ident[EI_CLASS]: 32 (ELFCLASS32) or 64
27	// (ELFCLASS64). Returns 0 when `elf_path` is unreadable or not an ELF. Reads
28	// only the 16-byte e_ident (the class-independent prefix), so it answers for
29	// rv32 and rv64 alike -- the source of truth for the fast auto-pick of
30	// qemu-system-riscv32/64 and the cycle/hybrid arch-match guard.
31	int elf_xlen(const std::string& elf_path);
32	
33	// L26/F3: the highest byte of the ELF's static memory image -- the maximum
34	// (p_paddr + p_memsz) over PT_LOAD segments. The driver rejects a hybrid run
35	// when this exceeds the V-scratch GPA (ram_base + --mem-size): the static image
36	// would extend into the reserved transport page above the program's RAM.
37	// Returns 0 + err on an unreadable / non-ELFCLASS64 file; 0 with empty err when
38	// the ELF has no loadable segments (nothing to clash with the scratch).
39	uint64_t elf_load_top(const std::string& elf_path, std::string& err);
40	
41	// Reverse lookup: the nearest function symbol at or below `addr`, formatted
42	// "name+0xoff" (or just "name" at offset 0). Returns "" when no covering
43	// function symbol is found or the ELF is unreadable -- the caller always has
44	// the raw pc to fall back on, so this never errors.
45	std::string symbolize(const std::string& elf_path, uint64_t addr);
46

content.text: Review complete. Findings below cover the driver command/infra layer scope.

findings.title: read_hybrid_toolchain hand-rolls a second config.env parser; the same key is resolved elsewhere via config_env_value
findings.detail: cmd_doctor.cpp carries ~45 lines of private config.env parsing (strip_char at line 41, parse_toolchain_line at 146, read_hybrid_toolchain at 175) just to resolve HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN, while the same binary already resolves the SAME key with the shared helper config_env_value("HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN") in manifest.cpp:86 and cmd_profile.cpp:76 (config_env.hpp:22). The two parsers diverge: doctor's accepts `export KEY = "value"` (optional export keyword, whitespace around '=', double-then-single quote stripping), config_env_value accepts only plain `KEY=value`. So today doctor can report the toolchain PASS from an `export`-style line that `--runtime linux` staging and `profile` then fail to resolve. The comment at line 145 says it "mirrors hsim._read_hybrid_toolchain" -- the deleted Python driver (no *hsim* files exist in the repo), confirming this is a carried-over port, and config_env.hpp:5's own comment claims it matches "how cmd_doctor already resolves HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN", which is no longer exactly true. Collapse to one parser: replace read_hybrid_toolchain's file branch with config_env_value("HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN") and delete strip_char/parse_toolchain_line.
findings.safety: On the documented config.env format (plain KEY=value; config.env.example line 13 ships exactly that, no export/quotes) both parsers return identical values, so doctor's rows are unchanged. Behavior differs only for export/quoted lines -- inputs the binary's other two consumers of the same key already cannot parse, so unifying makes doctor consistent rather than silently more permissive. If byte-exact preservation on exotic lines is required, the alternative is hoisting doctor's permissive parser into config_env.hpp for all three callers; either way the duplicate parser goes away.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f3.sh (doctor section/exit-code contract) and tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh (profile resolves $HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's objdump).

findings.title: fn_range duplicates symbolize's covering-FUNC-symbol scan
findings.detail: symbolize (elf_syms.cpp:159-213) and fn_range (215-246) both walk every SHT_SYMTAB section and run the identical candidate-selection predicate (SHN_UNDEF skip, STT_FUNC only, st_value <= addr, size-covered-or-preceding-label, best_value monotonic) -- lines 186-193 and 231-237 are byte-for-byte the same logic, ~30 duplicated lines. The only differences: symbolize also resolves the name through str_sh (and REJECTS a candidate whose name offset is out of bounds/unterminated, lines 195-199), while fn_range never loads str_sh at all and keeps size. Extract one static helper (e.g. find_covering_func(buf, eh, addr, need_name) -> {value, size, name}) used by both.
findings.safety: Behavior-preserving only if the helper gates the string-table lookup and the bad-name rejection on need_name: symbolize skips unnamed/corrupt-name candidates and skips symtabs with an invalid sh_link, fn_range accepts them -- the helper must keep that divergence (a need_name flag does it exactly). With that, both functions' outputs are bit-identical on every input, including malformed ELFs.
findings.verify_with: build with -Wall/-Wextra plus andesim-elf-syms-test and andesim-hybrid-test (both link elf_syms.cpp); end-to-end via tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_profile.sh, whose report exercises symbolize+fn_range on real ELFs (cmd_profile.cpp:200-204).

findings.title: unsupported_written_warning hand-rolls a comma join that strutil.hpp already provides
findings.detail: state_diff.cpp:254-258 builds the names string with a manual `if (!names.empty()) names += ", "; names += n;` loop. strutil.hpp:35 defines join(const std::vector<std::string>&, const char* sep) producing exactly the same output; it is already used for the same purpose in cmd_doctor.cpp:267 and engine_registry.hpp:88. Replace the 5-line loop with join(bad, ", ") plus an #include "strutil.hpp".
findings.safety: join() with sep=", " produces byte-identical output for every input (including the empty and single-element cases -- the function returns early on empty `bad` before this code runs). Pure textual substitution, header-only helper, no behavior change.
findings.verify_with: andesim-state-diff-test: state_diff_test.cpp:417-425 asserts unsupported_written_warning's exact output.

findings.title: Compare-policy comment claims medeleg/mideleg/satp are always skipped; the code conditionally compares them
findings.detail: state_diff.hpp:12-15 says "skipped: mstatus, mtvec, medeleg, mideleg, mip, satp... mtvec/medeleg/mideleg/satp are passthrough on the vsim side (copied from QEMU1's ENTRY snapshot, never re-read)". state_diff.cpp:57-63 contradicts this: since the ax66 registration (option A, also documented in CLAUDE.md's CSR-restore-split section) satp/medeleg/mideleg ARE compared whenever the engine's --describe andes_csrs list names them (`if (in_list("satp")) cmp(...)` etc.), because on S-mode-capable engines they are restored and re-read. The header's policy summary is the documented contract readers rely on and it is now wrong for S-mode engines.
findings.safety: Comment-only edit (move medeleg/mideleg/satp from the unconditional 'skipped' list to a 'compared when the engine's andes_csrs names them' clause). No code changes, no behavior change.
findings.verify_with: Recompile (comment-only); andesim-state-diff-test still passes; tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_verify.sh exercises the live compare path.

findings.title: References to "the state-diff subcommand" -- a command that no longer exists
findings.detail: state_diff.hpp:49 ("Empty = no engine info -> compare every Andes CSR (the state-diff subcommand and unit tests)") and :54 ("Shared by the state-diff subcommand and run --verify") both cite an `andesim state-diff` subcommand. It was removed: cli.cpp:29-32's is_subcommand admits only run/list/doctor/profile, main.cpp:35-36 says state-diff tooling lives in scripts, and tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh:42-68 explicitly asserts `state-diff` is NOT dispatchable. The only production consumers of diff_states/print_diff_report are cmd_run.cpp:722-723 (run --verify).
findings.safety: Comment-only edit (drop the subcommand mentions; the real consumers are run --verify and the unit tests). No behavior change.

findings.title: Dispatch comment says parse_cli yields only run/list/doctor -- omits profile
findings.detail: main.cpp:33-36: "so parse_cli only ever yields run/list/doctor (or \"\" for no args / top-level help)". cli.cpp:29-32's is_subcommand also admits "profile", and main.cpp itself dispatches it at line 229 (and the later comment at line 181 correctly says "parse_cli admits only run/list/doctor/profile"). The two comments in the same file disagree; the first predates the profile subcommand.
findings.safety: Comment-only edit (add profile to the list). No behavior change.
findings.verify_with: Recompile; tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_f0.sh (usage smoke) and test_andes_sim_profile.sh (profile dispatch).

findings.title: dry_run field comment names removed subcommands "build, run, test"
findings.detail: cli.hpp:50: `bool dry_run = false; // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)`. The binary has no build or test subcommands -- is_subcommand (cli.cpp:29-32) admits only run/list/doctor/profile, and tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh:42-57 asserts build/test are not dispatchable ("The former developer commands build/test/state-diff" moved to scripts). --dry-run today applies to run (fast/cycle/hybrid) and profile, per main.cpp's kRunOpts:80 and kProfileOpts:144.
findings.safety: Comment-only edit (e.g. "--dry-run (run, profile)"). No behavior change.

findings.title: OptRow::dev is never true -- the dev-filter branch in print_run_block is unreachable
findings.detail: OptRow (main.cpp:67-72) has `bool dev` documented as "hides it unless ANDESIM_DEV is set" (line 66), and print_run_block filters on it (line 118: `if (o.dev && !is_dev_mode()) continue;`). But every row in kRunOpts (lines 74-90) and kProfileOpts (lines 134-145) initializes dev=false, so the filter never skips anything -- and the kProfileOpts print loop (line 153) does not even consult dev. Contrast TargetRow::dev, which IS live (kListTargets' fixtures row, line 61). The field, its initializers, and the line-118 branch are dead.
findings.safety: With no dev=true row, deleting the field, the 28 trailing `false` initializers, and the line-118 check produces byte-identical help output in both dev and non-dev mode. If the field is instead kept as deliberate future surface, at minimum the kProfileOpts loop should honor it -- but as-is nothing exercises it.
findings.verify_with: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_release_surface.sh (asserts the exact help surface with and without ANDESIM_DEV) and test_andes_sim_f0.sh.

findings.title: Cli::has_passthrough is written by the parser but read by no production code
findings.detail: cli.cpp:58 sets has_passthrough=true at the `--` boundary, and cli.hpp:64 declares it, but a repo-wide grep finds readers only in cli_test.cpp (lines 27/47/58/222/315). The one place that cares whether engine args were passed -- cmd_run.cpp:804's hybrid rejection -- tests `!cli.passthrough.empty()` instead, and every other consumer (cmd_run.cpp:151/222/307/546, cmd_profile.cpp:337) uses the passthrough vector directly. The bare-`--`-with-no-args distinction the flag could encode is used by nothing.
findings.safety: No production read means removing the field and its cli.cpp:58 assignment (plus the corresponding cli_test CHECKs) cannot change any product behavior; the parser's observable output (subcommand/options/positional/passthrough) is untouched. Alternatively keep it and leave this as documentation-of-intent -- but then it should gain a comment saying it is parser-metadata for tests only.
findings.verify_with: andesim-cli-test (after dropping its has_passthrough CHECKs), andesim-run-test (F7 passthrough argv assembly), tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_dry_run.sh (`--` forwarding).
